MotivicEtaleKTheory.summary: Apart from low-degree Galois-cohomological ingredients, none of this roadmap exists: neither library has Milnor K-theory or any K-theory above K_0, higher Chow groups or cycle complexes, motivic cohomology, finite correspondences, Nisnevich sheaves or motivic categories, motivic operations, norm varieties or Rost motives, the motivic spectral sequence, etale K-theory, rigidity, Quillen-Lichtenbaum, etale Chern classes, Deligne cohomology, local or global Galois duality, or Selmer complexes, so all fourteen layers are not built. What the libraries do have: Mathlib's continuous cohomology of topological representations in all degrees, the p-adic cyclotomic character, the small etale and pro-etale sites of a scheme with Ext-based sheaf cohomology and untwisted l-adic cohomology H^i(X, Z_l), Hilbert 90 for finite Galois extensions, Tate cohomology of finite groups, algebraic cycles with pushforward, Picard groups, the weight-one unit regulator, Euler polynomials of elliptic curves from point counts, and abstract spectral sequences of spectral objects; Tau Ceti's explicit low-degree continuous cohomology with corestriction, cup products and the injective Kummer map K^x/(K^x)^n -> H^1(G_K, mu_n), cyclic Tate periodicity, line-bundle classes, determinant lines of free modules and 2-Selmer groups of elliptic curves. These give the degree-one case of the norm-residue theorem only up to the missing profinite Hilbert 90, and the cup product of Kummer classes needed for the Galois symbol in M.3, but no Steinberg relation. Most coefficient and duality targets in M.1-M.2 are restatements of ArithmeticGaloisDuality D7/R02, and the symbol comparison in M.3 is shared with K2SymbolsBrauer T.7.

targets.target: Finite and continuous Tate-twist coefficient modules mu_(l^r)^(x)j and Z_l(j), and Q/Z(j) via primewise compatible twists
targets.note: Only the weight-one pieces exist: Tau Ceti's discrete G_K-module mu_n and Mathlib's p-adic and mod p^k cyclotomic characters of a field automorphism. Tensor-power twists j != 1, the compact module Z_l(j) and the primewise Q/Z(j) are absent.

targets.target: Continuous Galois cohomology with finite, compact and discrete coefficients and derived inverse limits (imported from ArithmeticGaloisDuality)
targets.note: Mathlib defines continuous cohomology of any topological representation in all degrees (so compact coefficients are admissible), and Tau Ceti has an explicit low-degree model with long exact sequences; for schemes Mathlib defines l-adic cohomology H^i(X, Z_l) as pro-etale cohomology of the sheaf of continuous Z_l-valued maps (untwisted, with no comparison to etale cohomology yet). Derived inverse limits, lim^1 and the comparison of continuous cohomology with the limit of finite-coefficient cohomology are absent.

targets.target: Small etale sites of schemes and the comparison of etale cohomology of a field or S-integer ring with Galois cohomology
targets.note: Mathlib has the small etale site of a scheme with geometric points, proves its sheaf categories Grothendieck abelian, and defines sheaf cohomology on any site as Ext, so etale cohomology groups exist as a carrier; nothing computes them, and there is no comparison with Galois cohomology for Spec of a field or of S-integers.

targets.note: Absent; there is no K-theory above K_0 and no etale Chern class.

Defines W_j(F) = H^0(F, Q/Z(j)) from the cyclotomic character, using the same primewise Q/Z(j) twist M.1 specifies.

Polylogarithms.summary: Neither library contains a polylogarithm beyond Li_1: there is no Li_n for n >= 2, no dilogarithm or Bloch-Wigner function, no Bloch group or polylogarithmic complex, no weight-two or weight-three regulator, no Zagier-type statement, no p-adic logarithm and no statement of Leopoldt's conjecture, so every layer is not built. What exists is analytic and arithmetic input: Mathlib's series sum z^n/n = -log(1-z) on the unit disk (the n = 1 case of P.1's definition), the complex logarithm and argument with the slit plane, Bernoulli polynomials and their Fourier series (which give Li_k(e^(2 pi i x)) + (-1)^k Li_k(e^(-2 pi i x)) as a Bernoulli polynomial, the unit-circle case of the inversion formula), the weight-one unit regulator, discriminant and Dedekind zeta function, and exterior powers; Tau Ceti adds function-field places with residues of units and local unit filtrations. P.2-P.6 also wait on Bloch groups (K3BlochGroups), Borel regulators and motivic cohomology, none of which exist.

targets.target: Li_n(z) as the convergent power series sum z^k/k^n on the unit disk, with its differentiation formula
targets.note: Only n = 1 is present: Mathlib proves that sum z^n/n converges to -log(1 - z) for |z| < 1. No Li_n for n >= 2, and no z d/dz Li_n = Li_(n-1) recursion.

targets.target: Analytic continuation of Li_n to a specified cut domain and branch-change formulas
targets.note: Mathlib has the slit plane and the principal logarithm (hence the continuation of Li_1), and proves that sum (e(nx) + (-1)^k e(-nx))/n^k = -(2 pi i)^k/k! B_k(x) for x in [0,1], k >= 2, which is the unit-circle boundary case of the polylogarithm inversion formula; no continuation of Li_n and no monodromy/branch-change formula.

targets.target: Distribution relations for Li_n
targets.note: Absent from both libraries.

targets.target: Single-valued real polylogarithms with the Bernoulli coefficients and parity convention of the source
targets.note: Bernoulli numbers, Bernoulli polynomials and the periodised Bernoulli functions exist in Mathlib, but no single-valued polylogarithm D_n or L_n is defined.

targets.target: Continuous extensions of the single-valued functions at 0, 1 and infinity
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: The Bloch-Wigner dilogarithm D(z) = Im Li_2(z) + arg(1 - z) log|z| on a cut domain, single-valued and independent of the presentation
targets.note: Mathlib's Complex.arg is the principal argument (discontinuous on the negative real axis), which is exactly why the roadmap forbids treating arg as globally continuous; no dilogarithm is defined.

targets.target: Conjugation, inversion, five-term identity and differential formula for D, with boundary values and logarithmic singularities handled explicitly
targets.note: Absent; the phrase 'five-term' occurs in the libraries only in docstrings about the inflation-restriction sequence of group cohomology.

RefinedTraceMethods.summary: Nothing trace-theoretic exists in either library: 'Hochschild' occurs only in a TODO about the Hochschild-Serre spectral sequence, and there are no cyclic or mixed complexes, Connes' B, HKR, THH, circle actions or Tate constructions on spectra, cyclotomic spectra, TC, TC^- or TP, Dennis or cyclotomic traces, topological K-theory or ku/KU, q-de Rham or q-Hodge complexes, localizing motives, prismatic or syntomic objects, so every layer is not built. The algebraic inputs are in Mathlib: simplicial objects with the alternating face map complex, Moore normalisation and Dold-Kan, total complexes of bicomplexes, Tor in monoidal abelian categories, Kaehler differentials and exterior powers, Morita equivalence, Tate cohomology of finite groups (the algebraic shadow of the Tate construction, which Tau Ceti extends with Herbrand quotients and periodicity for cyclic groups), p-typical Witt vectors with Frobenius and Verschiebung, topological vector bundles, and Fontaine's theta; Tau Ceti adds real Clifford-algebra Bott periodicity. RT.1 is the only layer that could be started directly on these foundations; the rest need spectra from StableHomotopyKTheory and K-theory from GeneralAlgebraicKTheory first.

SchemeKTheoryOperations.summary: The libraries have the abelian and geometric substrate but no K-theory of schemes. Mathlib supplies sheaves of modules on a scheme as an abelian category with the pullback/pushforward adjunction, locally free, finite-type, quasi-coherent and finitely presented sheaves, the tilde functor, complexes with quasi-isomorphisms and derived categories, Proj, affine space, algebraic cycles with pushforward, Picard groups, regular rings as a definition and Mayer-Vietoris squares for Grothendieck topologies; Tau Ceti adds finitely presented sheaves on schemes, cohomology of sheaves of modules with Mayer-Vietoris and truncated Euler characteristics, line bundles, Weil divisors with an injective class-group-to-line-bundle map on regular curves, Riemann-Roch for function fields, the DG enrichment of complexes, exact and triangulated K_0, and the degree-zero affine Cartan map K_0(proj R) -> G_0(mod R) with its inverse under finite projective resolutions. Genuinely missing: perfect complexes on schemes and any enhancement, K(X) and G(X) with derived pullback and proper pushforward, supports, the localisation sequence and devissage, Zariski/Nisnevich descent, coniveau and Gersten, homotopy invariance, the projective-bundle, fundamental and blow-up theorems (no blow-ups of schemes at all), homotopy K-theory, products, lambda- and Adams operations, Chern classes, the Chern character, the gamma-filtration, Chow groups and Grothendieck-Riemann-Roch. S.1 (complexes and quasi-isomorphisms) and S.7 (cycles and divisors) are the only partly built layers.

targets.target: Complexes of sheaves of modules on a scheme and quasi-isomorphisms, from the existing sheaf and homological-complex categories
targets.note: X.Modules is Mathlib's abelian category of sheaves of modules on X (SheafOfModules is proved abelian), so HomologicalComplex X.Modules with QuasiIso, the quasi-isomorphism morphism property and the derived category are available directly.

targets.target: Perfect complexes defined locally as bounded complexes of finite locally free sheaves
targets.note: Local freeness and finite type of a single sheaf of modules are defined in Mathlib, but there is no strictly perfect or perfect complex: the phrase 'perfect complex' occurs nowhere in either library.

targets.target: Locality of perfectness, closure under shifts, cones and retracts, and stability under pullback
targets.note: Only the underived pullback of sheaves of modules exists; no perfect complexes to which these closure properties could apply.

targets.target: Essential smallness of perfect complexes on quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: An enhanced (dg or infinity-categorical) model of perfect complexes suitable for K-theory
targets.note: Tau Ceti enriches cochain complexes over a linear category in their Hom complexes, which is the DG category of complexes, but there is no DG nerve, pretriangulated hull, DG quotient or enhancement of perfect complexes on a scheme.

targets.target: Affine comparison of perfect complexes on Spec A with perfect complexes of A-modules
targets.note: Mathlib's tilde functor from A-modules to sheaves of modules on Spec A (fully faithful, left adjoint to global sections) is the degreewise input; perfect complexes of A-modules are also absent.

targets.target: Comparison with globally bounded complexes of vector bundles under a proved resolution property
targets.note: No resolution property for schemes is defined.

duplicates.note: Constructs the unbounded dg category of complexes of module sheaves with K-injective/K-flat replacements and the enhanced pullback/pushforward adjunction, overlapping S.1's enhancement and pullback targets.
Defines perfectness of complexes of modules through local finite projective resolutions (over complete Noetherian local algebras), the module-level notion S.1's affine comparison needs.

targets.target: K(X) as the K-theory of perfect complexes
targets.note: No K-theory space or spectrum of any category exists; Tau Ceti's exact and triangulated K_0 would give K_0(X) once a small perfect category existed, but perfect complexes are absent too.

targets.target: G(X) as the K-theory of coherent sheaves on a noetherian scheme
targets.note: Tau Ceti packages finitely presented sheaves on a scheme (the coherent objects on a locally Noetherian scheme) as a full subcategory, without an exact structure or K-group; its truncated Euler characteristic of a sheaf over a field, additive on short exact sequences under vanishing hypotheses, is the kind of invariant G_0 would factor. No G-theory.

targets.target: Derived pullback on perfect complexes for arbitrary morphisms
targets.note: Only the underived pullback/pushforward adjunction on sheaves of modules exists; there are no derived functors on complexes of sheaves on schemes.

targets.target: Proper pushforward on G-theory, and pushforward on K-theory for proper perfect morphisms
targets.note: Only the underived pushforward of sheaves of modules exists; no higher direct images, coherence of direct images or perfect morphisms.

targets.target: Flat base change, projection formula, composition and affine scalar-extension/restriction comparisons
targets.note: Absent for sheaves on schemes and for K-theory.

targets.target: The Cartan map K(X) -> G(X), an equivalence for regular noetherian finite-dimensional schemes
targets.note: Tau Ceti proves the degree-zero affine case: the Cartan map K_0(proj R) -> G_0(mod R) of any ring, and its inverse whenever every finitely generated module has a finite resolution by finitely generated projectives, sorry-free. Missing: the scheme and higher-degree versions, and the fact that regular Noetherian rings satisfy the resolution hypothesis (Mathlib defines IsRegularRing but has no Auslander-Buchsbaum-Serre theorem).

duplicates.note: Constructs K-theory pullback for arbitrary scheme morphisms and pushforward for proper perfect morphisms with projection formulas, the same functoriality targets as S.2.

Owns the Cartan map K_0(proj A) -> G_0(mod A) and its inverse under finite projective resolutions, the affine degree-zero case that Tau Ceti has already built.

targets.note: Absent; neither perfect complexes nor supports of complexes exist.

targets.note: Absent from both libraries.

targets.note: No exact-category (Quillen) localisation theorem exists either; Tau Ceti's exact K_0 has no localisation sequence.

targets.note: Absent.

Missing: the K-theoretic boundary maps, tame symbols (no K_2), curves and arithmetic surfaces.

targets.note: Points with their (co)heights are used for Mathlib's algebraic cycles and Tau Ceti's codimension-one points, but there is no filtration of K-theory by codimension of support and no exact couple.

targets.target: Gersten results for smooth varieties over fields and for the explicit arithmetic local rings, with separate mixed-characteristic hypotheses

Constructs the support categories and homotopy-coniveau tower on K-theory spectra, overlapping S.4's codimension filtration.

targets.target: Homotopy invariance K(X x A^1) = K(X) for regular noetherian schemes
targets.note: Mathlib defines affine space over a scheme; no K-theory and no homotopy-invariance statement.

targets.note: Mathlib has the Proj construction and Tau Ceti invertible sheaves, but there is no projective bundle of a vector bundle, no O(1) on it and no K-theory decomposition.

targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: External products on K-theory of schemes, with supports and relative theories, graded commutativity and compatibility with flat pullback and proper pushforward
targets.note: Tau Ceti makes split K_0 of a monoidal preadditive category a ring (commutative when braided); there are no products on higher K-groups or on K-theory of schemes.

targets.note: Neither library has lambda-rings or lambda-operations (a Mathlib docstring notes that Mathlib does not know what a lambda-ring is); exterior powers of modules exist but give no operations on K-theory.

targets.note: Absent from both libraries.

targets.target: Eigenvalue psi^k = k^j on weight-j rational K-theory and rational projectors from finitely many Adams operations
targets.note: Absent.

targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Scheme divisor and cycle constructions shared with AlgebraicCurves/JacobianChallenge
targets.note: Mathlib defines algebraic cycles on a scheme as locally finite functions on points, with pushforward along quasi-compact morphisms; Tau Ceti defines Weil divisors as codimension-one cycles with principal divisors and linear equivalence and, on Noetherian integral schemes of dimension at most one with DVR local rings, an injective map from the divisor class group to line-bundle classes. targets.note: Absent; no projective or flag bundles of vector bundles on schemes.

StableHomotopyKTheory.summary: Mathlib already supplies the simplicial and categorical starting points: the nerve of a category with the map induced by a functor (fully faithful and right adjoint to the homotopy-category functor), geometric realisation SSet.toTop left adjoint to the singular simplicial set, Kan complexes, CW complexes, perfect groups, group homology via the bar complex, EG as a simplicial G-set, and abstract spectral sequences of spectral objects; Tau Ceti adds the topological homotopy-group layer (functoriality, basepoint change and the pi_1-action, homotopy invariance, the loop-space shift, covering isomorphisms, K(G,1) recognition), local coefficient systems on the fundamental groupoid, and the identification of split K_0 with the Grothendieck group of the monoid of isomorphism classes. Genuinely missing: homotopies induced by natural transformations and contractibility for categories with initial or terminal objects, BG as a K(G,1) and its bar/singular comparison, topological homotopy fibres and the fibration long exact sequence, homotopy groups of Kan complexes and their comparison with topological ones, Quillen's Theorems A and B, the plus construction, Gamma-spaces and the group-completion theorem, any model of spectra with stable homotopy groups, smash products or the S-construction delooping, and the Bockstein sequence, lim^1/Milnor sequence and exact couples with convergence. Only H.1 is partly built; the Hurewicz theorem its tests need is also absent.

targets.target: Nerve of a small category and the simplicial map induced by a functor, compatible with identities and composition
targets.note: nerve C is the simplicial set of composable arrows and nerveFunctor : Cat => SSet packages functoriality; Mathlib also proves it fully faithful and right adjoint to the homotopy-category functor, so at the simplicial level it preserves limits such as products. The nerve lands in SSet.{max u v}.

targets.target: Geometric realisation of nerves and of the maps induced by functors
targets.note: Realisation is defined for every simplicial set and is left adjoint to the singular simplicial set, so |N C| and |N F| are available by composition with the nerve functor; no statement specific to nerves is needed for this target.

targets.target: Homotopy between realised maps induced by a natural transformation, and homotopy equivalence induced by an equivalence of categories
targets.note: Mathlib defines simplicial homotopies X (x) Delta[1] -> Y and turns them into combinatorial homotopies, but never builds one from a natural transformation (via N(C x [1]) = N C x Delta[1]) or deduces invariance of |N C| under equivalences of categories.

targets.target: Compatibility of classifying spaces with products and filtered diagrams of categories
targets.note: Only the simplicial part for limits follows from the adjunction hoFunctor -| nerveFunctor; missing are |N(C x D)| ~ |N C| x |N D| and the commutation of nerve and realisation with filtered colimits of categories. Mathlib has started the convenient category of X-generated spaces where the product statement would live, but its cartesian closed structure is still a TODO and nothing connects it to realisation.

targets.target: Contractibility of the classifying space of a category with an initial or terminal object
targets.note: No contractibility statement for nerves or their realisations exists in either library.

targets.target: Classifying space of a discrete group: the nerve of its one-object groupoid identified with the bar construction
targets.note: Mathlib builds EG = (G^(n+1))_n as a simplicial G-set (the Cech nerve of G -> pt) and the bar resolution/bar complex of group homology, but never forms BG, never takes the nerve of SingleObj G, and states no identification between them.

targets.target: The realisation of BG is a K(G,1), with the map on fundamental groups induced by a group homomorphism
targets.note: Tau Ceti defines the K(G,1) property (aspherical with pi_1 isomorphic to G), proves it basepoint-independent, stable under products and homotopy equivalence, and proves that the orbit space of a free properly discontinuous action on a simply connected aspherical space is a K(G,1); it also has the map induced on homotopy groups by a based map. Applying this to BG needs the realisation of the nerve of G and its universal cover, which is missing.

targets.target: Local coefficient systems
targets.note: Sorry-free: functors from Mathlib's fundamental groupoid to ModuleCat R, with constant systems, pullback along continuous maps, path transport, basepoint change and the monodromy representation. Singular chains with local coefficients are not built.

targets.target: Comparison of bar (group) homology, including local coefficients, with singular homology of BG
targets.note: Both homology theories exist separately (group homology from the inhomogeneous/bar complex, singular homology of a space), but there is no BG and no singular homology with local coefficients, so no comparison.

targets.target: Tests: BG of the trivial group is contractible; conjugate homomorphisms induce freely homotopic maps; the induced map on H_1 is abelianisation
targets.note: Algebraically Mathlib proves H_1(G,A) = G^ab (x) A for trivial coefficients, and Tau Ceti identifies free homotopy classes with orbits of the pi_1-action on pi_n; none of the three topological tests about BG can be stated without BG.

duplicates.note: Item 6 defines local coefficient systems as functors on the fundamental groupoid with pullback, basepoint change and monodromy (the target Tau Ceti has built as TauCeti.LocalCoefficientSystem) and also owns the twisted singular chains needed for the bar/singular comparison.

Item 14 owns K(G,1) recognition, products and homotopy invariance (built in Tau Ceti), and explicitly leaves constructing a K(G,1) for an arbitrary group to simplicial realisation theory, which is H.1's BG target.

targets.target: Homotopy fibres and homotopy pullbacks of maps of spaces, with their naturality
targets.note: The only homotopy fibre in either library is the one for morphisms of homological complexes; for spaces there is no mapping path space, homotopy fibre or homotopy pullback.

targets.target: Basepoint choices and change of basepoint for homotopy fibres and fibre sequences
targets.note: Tau Ceti proves change of basepoint for homotopy groups along a path (depending only on its homotopy class) and the action of pi_1 on pi_n by automorphisms, sorry-free; transport of homotopy fibres and of fibre sequences along paths in the base is missing.

targets.target: Long exact sequence of homotopy groups of a fibre sequence, with the pointed-set/group distinction in degrees 0 and 1
targets.note: No boundary map pi_n(B) -> pi_(n-1)(F) and no exactness statement exists for any fibration; Tau Ceti proves only the covering-map consequence p_* : pi_n(E) = pi_n(X) for n >= 2 directly from homotopy lifting. Tau Ceti's long exact sequences are for relative singular homology of pairs and triples.

targets.target: Comparison of Kan-simplicial and topological homotopy groups
